item.title: Eight dead in traffic accident along Okuk highway
item.description: Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent Albert Beli has confirmed that eight people died in a traffic accident that occurred between 2:00 AM and 3:00 AM this morning at Itani Village, Asaro, along the Okuk Highway in Eastern Highlands Province. ​PPC Beli said, 13 people were allegedly traveling in the 10-seater vehicle downhill at Itani village when the vehicle ran off t
item.content:encoded:
Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent Albert Beli has confirmed that eight people died in a traffic accident that occurred between 2:00 AM and 3:00 AM this morning at Itani Village, Asaro, along the Okuk Highway in Eastern Highlands Province.

​PPC Beli said, 13 people were allegedly traveling in the 10-seater vehicle downhill at Itani village when the vehicle ran off the road, causing the crash.

​"Reports confirm that five males and three females died, while five others are currently seeking medical treatment. The vehicle involved is a white Toyota Land Cruiser bearing registration number SAF 033.

Police personnel have been deployed to assist at the accident scene," PPC Beli said.

​Asaro police officers and Highway Patrol personnel confirmed that the eight deceased individuals have been transferred to the Goroka Base Hospital morgue, while the remaining five are receiving medical treatment at the Asaro Health Centre.

Officers are currently working to establish the identities of the victims and the deceased.

​While commenting on the incident, PPC Beli emphasized that many traffic accidents reported along the highway could be avoided if drivers obeyed simple traffic rules.

He said that in the past, people respected traffic laws, resulting in fewer accidents compared to today

item.title: PM commends Central Gulf
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has commended the political leadership, landowners and communities of Gulf and Central Provinces for reaching a landmark agreement on the benefit sharing of Papua LNG project. Following months of negotiations, Gulf will receive 80 percent and Central 20 percent.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has commended the political leadership, landowners and communities of Gulf and Central Provinces for reaching a landmark agreement on the benefit sharing of Papua LNG project.

Following months of negotiations, Gulf will receive 80 percent and Central 20 percent.

In a statement , Marape described it as a milestone towards the project's targetted Final Investment Decision in December.

He says this demonstrates maturity , cooperation and a shared commitment to national development.

The agreement is consistent with the broad principles established under the existing PNG LNG Project , where benefits were distributed between upstream resource areas , downstream facilities and pipeline corridors.

It now enables Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina to bring the necessary submissions to National Executive Council for decisions on the distributions of project benefits.

These would increase infrastructure development grants , equity participation and other policy based benefits for Gulf and Central Provinces.

The Prime Minister also affirmed the government's policy, 40 percent of the State's equity participation must flow back to the provinces and landowners , where resources are developed.

item.title: Ward members emphasises more on recognition
item.description: Many ward members in Western Highlands say their role has not always received the recognition it deserves. This was the main issue discussed when 316 ward members from across Western Highlands gathered in Mt Hagen for their fourth Annual General Meeting recently.
item.content:encoded:
Many ward members in Western Highlands say their role has not always received the recognition it deserves.

This was the main issue discussed when 316 ward members from across Western Highlands gathered in Mt Hagen for their fourth Annual General Meeting recently.

Hosted by the Western Highlands Provincial Government, the AGM has been held every year since Governor Wai Rapa took office.

And for the ward members, it has become an important place to come together, share their experiences and speak about the challenges they face.

The ward is the grassroots level of Papua New Guinea's government system.

It is where national and provincial policies eventually reach the people.

But the people responsible for leading at that level often have very little resources to work with.

Hagen Open MP and Minister for State-Owned Enterprises William Duma, who opened the AGM, says ward members are elected representatives of the people.

"Ward members are elected by the people and they have a mandate from the people. They are representatives at the community and LLG level, and we must recognise the important work they do," Duma said.

Duma says many problems that later affect the district and province begin inside communities.

He added ward members are in the best position to deal with these problems before they become bigger.

"Many problems start at the community level. If they are not addressed there, they move to the township, the district and eventually the province gets the bad name."

He stressed that ward members may not have money, but they have something just as important-their voice and influence.

"You may not have money, but you have the power of speech. You have the influence to bring your people together and keep peace in your community, "MP Duma said.

Duma also acknowledged the ward members for coming together from their communities.

For them, the gathering carries a familiar cultural meaning.

In Melpa, “Mang Rapa” refers to a communal place where people come together, feel a sense of belonging and make important decisions for their community.

The AGM brought that same spirit into the formal government system.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa understands the ward level better than most.

Before becoming governor, he was a long-serving ward councillor himself.

He has also continued to raise ward members' issues at the national level.

Rapa says his government will continue working with the ward members.

"I have come from the ward level myself, so I understand the challenges our ward members face. They are very important to our communities, and our government will continue to work closely with them and support their work."

The message has also reached the national level.

Deputy Secretary Operations of the Department of Provincial and Local Level Government Affairs, Larsen Thomas, has attended the Western Highlands ward members' AGM for the past three years.

Thomas acknowledged Governor Rapa and the provincial government for giving ward members a stronger voice.

"For far too long, ward members have been missed out when it comes to government recognition. Western Highlands has given them a name and a voice, and that is something we acknowledge," Deputy Secretary Thomas acknowledged.

The department is now working on a strategy to provide greater support to ward members across the country.

One of the key initiatives is the K30,000 Ward Services Improvement Program, or Ward SIP.

"The K30,000 Ward SIP is part of the effort to strengthen the ward level. We want our elected ward representatives to have the support they need to respond to the needs of their communities."

item.title: Bushfire destroys rubber blocks and gardens in Delta Fly
item.description: Huge hectares of rubber blocks, food gardens and sago palms have been destroyed following a massive bushfire that swept through four villages in Delta Fly District of Western Province. The bush fire started last month and is continuing. The fire started at Kawito and spread to Pisi, Pikiwa and Paputa villages. Locals said the source of the fire is unknown.
item.content:encoded:
Huge hectares of rubber blocks, food gardens and sago palms have been destroyed following a massive bushfire that swept through four villages in Delta Fly District of Western Province. The bush fire started last month and is continuing.

The fire started at Kawito and spread to Pisi, Pikiwa and Paputa villages. Locals said the source of the fire is unknown.

Aramia LLG President and Deputy Governor for Western Province, Mr. Abini Gesele confirmed the bushfire. He told NBC News that thick smoke from the fire disturbed a MAF plane that attempted to land this week, but it later landed safely.

He urged people not to light fires in the bush during this dry period, saying it is very dangerous.

Meanwhile, another local said the fire dies down at night but flares up again when the sun picks up between 10am and 12pm.

No casualties have been reported; however, food gardens and sago palms were destroyed and affected families who depend on rubber and gardens for food and income are now calling for assistance.

item.title: NRL defends PNG Chiefs
item.description: The National Rugby League in Australia stand ready to defend New Zealand’s High Court injunction to stop NRL’s incoming franchise PNG Chiefs from using the Chiefs name. NRL Chairman Peter V’Landys says they will be defending the matter vigorously.
item.content:encoded:
The National Rugby League in Australia stand ready to defend New Zealand’s High Court injunction to stop NRL’s incoming franchise PNG Chiefs from using the Chiefs name.

NRL Chairman Peter V’Landys says they will be defending the matter vigorously.

“The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that,” V’Landys said.

“Rugby Union is obviously feeling threatened by Rugby League in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most Rugby League games.”

New Zealand Rugby mentioned in a statement this week saying it is seeking both an interim and final injunction to stop the use of the name "PNG Chiefs", "Chiefs" or any other similar names in New Zealand.

Meanwhile the PNG Chiefs official are set to officially announce its official logo on October 21st.

The PNG Chiefs also stated that they will not comment further on this matter, because it is an ongoing legal matter, and they are focused on launching their logo on the set dates.

Radio New Zealand reported that the Chiefs Super Rugby club have argued that allowing another professional sporting franchise to use the same name in the same trans-Tasman market risks undermining a brand it has spent three decades building.

item.title: Thousands of fish dead in Middle Fly lagoons
item.description: Manda Village in the Middle Fly District of Western Province has reported the worst fish kill in its history, with community leaders saying the current El Niño has killed hundreds of thousands of fish and is worse than the 2015 drought. Community leader Raynard Loka said the deaths started in September and became worse in early October
item.content:encoded:
Manda Village in the Middle Fly District of Western Province has reported the worst fish kill in its history, with community leaders saying the current El Niño has killed hundreds of thousands of fish and is worse than the 2015 drought.

Community leader Raynard Loka said the deaths started in September and became worse in early October

"This is the first time we have seen anything like this. In 2015 we never experienced this many fish dying.

This year's El Niño is worse plenty fish died, hundreds of thousands," Mr. Loka said.

Dead and rotten fish can be seen continuously from the mouth of Kai Lagoon to the end of the lagoon, including Barramundi, Catfish, Saratoga, Prawns, freshwater turtles and other small fish.

The community depends on for food and cash income from markets across Indonesia.

Meanwhile, Fly Zibo LLG Manager Noel Kaiyun told NBC News that two more lagoons have been hit but have not been reported.

He revealed that Agu Lagoon in Kuem and Mipan villages and Bai Lagoon in Wangawanga village have faced similar mass deaths, with lagoon systems now shallow, warm and trapped with no oxygen flow.

Affected villagers are now calling for urgent assistance and monitoring as more fish continue to die.

item.title: UOG embracing reforms through partnership
item.description: The University of Goroka is embracing reforms in all aspects. John Sari, a senior member of the University's Governing Council, emphasized this whilst addressing graduates at the recent graduation of the Madang Institute of Distant and Flexible Learning.
item.content:encoded:
The University of Goroka is embracing reforms in all aspects.

John Sari, a senior member of the University's Governing Council, emphasized this whilst addressing graduates at the recent graduation of the Madang Institute of Distant and Flexible Learning.

The graduation was held in Madang, a first out- of- campus ceremony for the IDFL.

Mr. Sari said that the graduation was a historical moment for the institute and for UOG, and commended the Madang Government and its administration, plus other departments who have understood and helped pillar number 8 come into fruition.

"On behalf of the university's Chancellor Joe Wemin and the university council, I commend the Madang Provincial Government and Governor Ramsey Pariwa for the partnership that UOG has established with Madang through a Memorandum of Understanding that was signed in May this year.

"The university is creating partnerships with various sectors, including church organisations and non-government agencies under the reforms. The University of Goroka has 10 reform pillars, and one of them is partnership.

"UOG is strongly embracing Partnership in all aspects, but at this juncture, I am looking at educational partnership. You know Human Resources is very important.

"UOG has embraced partnerships not only in the country but overseas as well. The physical developments on campus are testament of these partnerships because we have a roadmap, a vision, and a strategic plan that's resource- focus," he said.

Mr. Sari also told the graduates that they must be proud that they are privileged to be part of a premier institution that is moving forward.

Under Partnership number 8, Partnership, Linkages, and Collaborations, UOG intends to elevate its educational standards and secure global opportunities for its students.

It is also building its international academic benchmarking and accreditation through partnerships with major universities in the region, including China, India, Singapore, and the Philippines.

Pro- Vice Chancellor, Academic, Research and Innovation, Dr. Matthew Landu reiterated that the University of Goroka is serious about the reforms.

"In terms of infrastructure development, we want the best. We also want the best educational content for our students, and we work closely with the Department of Education and Higher Education to bring the students' level up. We must be internationally competent as well. With the best resources provided, we can do it," Dr. Landu said.

The University of Goroka is keen on reaching out to the unfortunate ones who cannot make it into universities after grade 12 through the IDFL to help them upgrade

item.title: Women researchers complete Lae training
item.description: Twelve women researchers have completed a four-day training in Lae to strengthen their research skills and improve the quality of their work. The training ended on Thursday, October 8, at Lae International Hotel under the Australian Government-supported Strongim Risets Kapasiti Bilong Ol Meri (SRKBOM) program.
item.content:encoded:
Twelve women researchers have completed a four-day training in Lae to strengthen their research skills and improve the quality of their work.

The training ended on Thursday, October 8, at Lae International Hotel under the Australian Government-supported Strongim Risets Kapasiti Bilong Ol Meri (SRKBOM) program.

The workshop covered data analysis, research methods, interviewing and reviewing existing studies.

Australian Consul-General Brenton Kanowski said women researchers played an important role in producing evidence to guide decisions and shape policies.

“When women help frame the questions, lead the inquiry and present the evidence, decision-making becomes stronger and more representative,” Mr Kanowski said.

He said Australia was proud to support women’s leadership and research capacity in Papua New Guinea.

Earlier this year, the 12 researchers spent a month in Brisbane and Melbourne to gain experience in the Australian academic environment.

The program also has groups in Port Moresby and Goroka.

A women’s research alumni network was scheduled to launch in Port Moresby on October 9 to help participants maintain professional connections and share knowledge.

item.title: International cocoa/chocolate experts visit Amazon Bay
item.description: ‎At least ten international Cocoa and chocolate experts are in the country visiting local cocoa farmers, this week, in the Amazon Bay in Central Province, accompanied by PNGs own Queen Emma Chocolate of Paradise Food industry General Manager, Karina Makori. ‎ ‎The team arrived in Alotau, Milne Bay Province, over the weekend before travelling by road and motorboat to Amazon Bay. ‎ ‎This is the second cocoa tourism adventure by international experts to PNG, aimed at giving the cocoa tourist first-hand experience about rural cocoa farming.
